citation: Chattopadhyay, De Sisternes and Oguah (2018). World Bank Electricity Planning Model mathematical formulation. ESMAP.
description: The Electricity Planning Model is a least-cost power-system planning tool developed by the World Bank Energy Sector Management Assistance Program. The project publishes GAMS source, public documentation and CSV input and output conventions. A planner supplies generating assets, hourly demand, technology costs, network zones and policy constraints. The model selects investments and dispatch while balancing costs, renewable targets, interconnections and carbon requirements. Outputs include capacity timing, zone-level generation and net present cost for the specified planning years. Geographic coverage follows the user's power-system zones. The repository advertises CC0-1.0 terms for its model material, but running it requires a compatible GAMS installation; the README says version 53 is tested and version 54 is not yet supported. A limitation is that large planning conclusions depend on input assumptions and the commercial solver environment. It supports utility and ministry capacity studies. The catalogue's model-pypsa is a separate open-source engine for comparison. No GAMS run was attempted.
inputs: Demand, generation, grid and technology-cost CSV inputs
